correctness.rationale: Universal equality of zero-delay FROG intensities for all independent complex Fourier coefficients gives coefficientwise equality of all same-sum unordered-pair phase products; the proof checks uniqueness of each mixed monomial and the converse for every delay. Three or more consecutive sites in each band force a constant adjacent phase ratio, cross-band adjacent equal sums force one common slope, and every remaining equality is exactly a meeting of two Minkowski pair-sum intervals. The displayed integer Smith matrix therefore classifies the entire universal gauge group. For two bands 2I and 2J are disjoint, leaving precisely two cross-overlap thresholds; counting their disjoint integer overlap intervals yields the exact phase-sensitive H. Two independent reproducible exact-integer finite tests and numerical traces passed, but the proof, not tests, establishes infinite quantifiers.

originality.rationale: No directly covering theorem was located in targeted semantic searches, relevant accessible prior claim comparison, and material inspection of the key FROG preprints and the closest published bispectral/fourth-moment results. The claim classifies universal diagonal phase multipliers of all-delay quartic FROG data for arbitrary unions of long integer bands, with a Smith-form group and a sharp two-band threshold. Existing FROG generic consecutive-band uniqueness, analytic-signal parity theorems, third-order bispectral phase fibers, and random-phase fourth-moment variance do not logically imply this specialized all-input invariance and threshold. A Freiman-homomorphism reformulation in older literature is a residual priority risk.
residual_risks: An equivalent all-input gauge result may exist in historical Freiman-2-homomorphism, additive combinatorics or experimental FROG literature under different vocabulary.
The 2017 initial FROG paper was inspected at abstract/model level only; coverage assessment does not depend on guessing its uninspected full content.
No independent worldwide literature priority verification is claimed.

value.rationale: The motivating reconstruction question is whether separate spectral bands have an invisible relative phase despite observing all frequency-resolved optical gating delays. The answer is a sharp information-theoretic obstruction over an infinite natural family, not a reparameterization of generic phase retrieval. The nontrivial general-band contribution is a complete Smith-invariant classification through an interval sum-overlap matrix, capturing resonances among three or more separated bands. The exact two-band boundary and H(a,b,c) quantify the onset and number of phase-sensitive Fourier rows. It does not claim reconstruction uniqueness when the obstruction vanishes, or any conditioning bound.
